name: ProgressBar
statusNote: Alpha in Primer React, accessibility-reviewed 2025-01-08. Its docs still list the default bg as 'bg.successInverse', a pre-token name; the code's default is 'success.emphasis'.
summary: A thin horizontal bar showing determinate progress, either one fill or several coloured segments (ProgressBar.Item) for a breakdown such as language shares. Use Spinner when progress is unknown.

inputs.name: progress
inputs.description: Percent filled, 0-100, for the single-fill form. Must not be combined with items.

inputs.name: bg
inputs.description: Fill colour as '<role>' or '<role>.<strength>', read as --bgColor-<role>-<strength> (strength defaults to emphasis).

inputs.name: inline
inputs.description: Inline instead of block; the caller must then give it a width.

inputs.name: animated
inputs.description: Shimmer the single fill (not items) to show ongoing work.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: ProgressBar.Item segments, each with progress, bg and an aria-label, laid side by side.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: aria-label for the single fill (or each item's own).

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: The full-width bar: --progressBar-track-bgColor with a 1px inset --progressBar-track-borderColor outline and a small radius, clipping its segments.

anatomy.name: Segment
anatomy.description: A fill as wide as its progress percent of the track, in --bgColor-<role>-<strength>; segments sit in order with 2px gaps, square-ended (the track's radius clips the ends).

variants.description: Any role the bgColor family has: success (default), accent, attention, severe, danger, done, sponsors, neutral, and so on, at emphasis unless a strength is given.

layout.text: The track is a flex row 8px tall (5px small, 10px large), as wide as its container (block) or as the caller sets (inline), with --borderRadius-small corners and its overflow clipped.
The track's border is a 1px solid --progressBar-track-borderColor outline offset -1px, drawn inside the box over its edge (transparent in the default theme).

Each segment's width is its progress as a percent of the track width; segments are separated by 2px gaps. Widths are not normalised: segments summing to 100% plus their gaps overflow and the last one is clipped.
bg 'role' or 'role.strength' maps to --bgColor-role-strength, strength defaulting to emphasis; no bg gives --bgColor-success-emphasis.

states.label: animated
states.text: animated, with no reduced-motion preference: the single fill's opacity is masked by a 75deg gradient (opaque to 30%, 65% opaque from 80%) twice the fill's width, which slides across it once per second, forever, with CSS's default ease curve. Under reduced motion there is no shimmer.

behaviour.text: Giving both progress and items is an error (the React component throws).
Progress is not clamped: a negative value draws nothing and over 100 is clipped by the track; the reported value is the rounded progress, or 0 when it is missing or negative.

The shimmer moves the mask from position 200% to 0%; with a mask twice the fill's width that is exactly one repeat, so the loop is seamless. The mask repeats (CSS default), so for fill width w and eased progress e in [0, 1) through each second, alpha(x) = g(((x / w - 2e) mod 2) / 2), where g(u) is 1 for u <= 0.3, falls linearly to 0.65 at u = 0.8 and stays 0.65 to u = 1; the pattern travels rightwards 2w per second. The 75deg angle tilts the bands slightly; on a bar 5-10px tall the tilt is negligible.

accessibility.role: progressbar (on each segment, not on the track)
semantics: Each segment has role progressbar, aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuenow the rounded progress (or the caller's value), optional aria-valuetext, and an aria-label.
The track itself has no role or name; a multi-segment bar is several progressbars, so label each.

notes.text: --progressBar-bgColor-<role> tokens exist for every role, but the component builds --bgColor-<role>-emphasis names instead and never reads them.
The docs give the default bg as 'bg.successInverse', which the code would turn into the non-existent --bgColor-bg-successInverse; the code's actual default is 'success.emphasis'.

Under forced colours the module redefines the track colour as CanvasText and the fill as LinkText at :root and opts both out of forced-colour adjustment. The fill override never wins because each segment sets its colour inline, and the track override only wins if no theme scope redefines the token below :root. A native build in a forced-colour mode should draw the track in the system text colour and the fill in the system link colour.
The shimmer is a CSS mask animation guarded by prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; a native build reads the platform's reduce-motion setting and skips it.
An inline bar has no intrinsic width (its segments are percentages of it), so it collapses to zero unless the caller sets a width.
Heights 5, 8 and 10px, the 2px gap, the 1px outline and the 1s shimmer are literals, not tokens.
